title_cn: 开往威斯特海温的快车
grammar_focus: too … to / … enough to do、can't help·can't stand·don't mind + 动名词、否定词句首倒装(Nor/Never/Hardly + 倒装)、passed 与 past 的区别、refuse 与 deny 的区别、borrow 与 lend 的区别(原创承载 NCE3 L37 考点·无需净化:一位乘客上了号称'快车'的火车,却站站慢吞吞,到站找站长投诉,才发现时刻表上一个小星号的脚注写着'此趟已停运'·温情自嘲喜剧;美式化 railroad/schedule/stationmaster)
scene: 我们早已习惯认定火车总是准点的。经过多年的耳濡目染,大多数人对铁路时刻表怀有一种不可动摇的信任。轮船可能因风暴而误点,航班可能因恶劣天气而取消,可火车必须准时。只有一场格外大的暴雪,才可能暂时打乱铁路运行。一出岔子,人们总是太容易去责怪铁路公司。事实上,出错的多半是我们自己,而不是他们。查过铁路时刻表后,我满意地发现有一趟开往威斯特海温的快车。它从我家附近的车站直达,全程只要一小时十七分钟。上车时,我忍不住注意到有许多本地人也上了车。当时,我并不觉得这有什么奇怪。我想,除了我以外,大概还有很多人想搭这趟出色的班车。火车在几英里外的小站威德利停下时,我也没觉得意外——再威风的快车也可能被信号灯拦住。可当火车站站都慢吞吞地停时,我开始纳闷了。我这才猛然醒悟:这趟快车根本没有以每小时九十英里的速度飞驰,而是勉强以三十英里的速度哐当哐当地爬。一小时十七分钟过去了,我们连一半路程都没走完。我问一位乘客,这是不是开往威斯特海温的快车,他却压根没听说过这趟车。我下定决心一到站就去投诉。两个小时后,我在威斯特海温站气冲冲地跟站长理论。他矢口否认有这趟车,我便借来他那本时刻表。当我告诉他白纸黑字明明写着时,声音里带着几分得意。他草草扫了一眼,让我再看仔细点。一个小小的星号把我引到页脚的一条注释,上面写着:“此趟班车已停运。”

grammar_card.title: too…to / enough to / can't help doing / 否定倒装 / passed vs past / refuse vs deny / borrow vs lend
grammar_card.intro: ①too + 形容词 + to do=“太…以致不能”;… enough to do=“足够…能”。②can't help / can't stand / don't mind 后接动名词:can't help noticing。③否定词(Never / Hardly / Nor / Little)放句首,句子要倒装(助动词提前)。④passed 是动词 pass 的过去式(时间过去了);past 是介词/形容词/名词(经过、过去的)。⑤refuse to do=拒绝做;deny=否认(某事、否认做过,后接动名词)。⑥borrow=(从别人那)借入;lend=把…借给别人。

rows: 过去/经过·拒绝/否认·借入/借出

specialRules.rule: passed 是动词(时间过去了:an hour passed);past 是介词/形容词/名词(rushed past;in times past)。别混。
borrow 是“借进来(向别人借)”:borrow sth from sb;lend 是“借出去(借给别人)”:lend sth to sb。方向相反。
美式:railroad(英式 railway)、schedule(英式 timetable)、stationmaster、conductor(英式 ticket collector)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What mistake did the writer make?
options: He overlooked a footnote saying the service was suspended
He forgot his ticket at home
He got off one stop too early

passage: We have learned to expect that trains will be punctual. After years of conditioning, most of us have developed an unshakable faith in railroad schedules. Ships may be delayed by storms; flights may be canceled because of bad weather; but trains must be on time. Only an exceptionally heavy snowfall might temporarily dislocate rail service. It is all too easy to blame the railroad company when something goes wrong. The truth is that when mistakes occur, they are more likely to be ours than theirs. After consulting my railroad schedule, I noted with satisfaction that there was an express train to Westhaven. It went direct from my local station, and the journey lasted a mere hour and seventeen minutes. When I boarded the train, I could not help noticing that a great many local people got on as well. At the time, this did not strike me as odd. I reflected that there must be many people besides myself who wished to take advantage of this excellent service. Nor was I surprised when the train stopped at Widley, a tiny station a few miles down the line. Even a mighty express can be held up by signals. But when the train dawdled at station after station, I began to wonder. It suddenly dawned on me that this express was not roaring down the line at ninety miles an hour, but barely chugging along at thirty. One hour and seventeen minutes passed, and we had not even covered half the distance. I asked a passenger whether this was the Westhaven Express, but he had never even heard of it. I resolved to lodge a complaint as soon as we arrived. Two hours later, I was talking angrily to the stationmaster at Westhaven. When he denied the train's existence, I borrowed his copy of the schedule. There was a note of triumph in my voice when I told him that it was there in black and white. Glancing at it briefly, he told me to look again. A tiny asterisk led me to a footnote at the bottom of the page. It said: 'This service has been suspended.'

grammar_points.name: can't help·can't stand·don't mind + 动名词
passed 与 past 的区别
refuse 与 deny 的区别
borrow 与 lend 的区别

stage5.stem: "It is all too easy ___ blame the railroad when a train is late."(too + 形容词 + ___ do)
stage5.stem_cn: 火车一晚点,人们太容易责怪铁路公司了。

stage5.stem: "The wall is too high ___ climb."(too + 形容词 + ___ + 动词,表"太…而不能")
"The step was low ___ for me to climb."("足够…以至能",该填哪个词)
"I could not help ___ that many locals got on the train."(can't help + 动名词"忍不住做")
stage5.stem_cn: 我忍不住注意到许多本地人也上了车。

stage5.stem: "I can't stand ___ for a delayed train."(can't stand + 动名词"受不了做")
stage5.stem_cn: 我受不了等一趟晚点的火车。

stage5.stem: "I don't mind ___ a little longer."(don't mind + 动名词"不介意做")
stage5.stem_cn: 我不介意再多等一会儿。

stage5.stem: "Nor ___ I surprised when the train stopped again."(否定词 nor 句首,要倒装)
stage5.stem_cn: 火车又停时,我也不感到意外。

stage5.stem: "Never ___ I seen such a slow express."(Never 句首,倒装用助动词提前)
stage5.stem_cn: 我从没见过这么慢的快车。

stage5.stem: "Hardly ___ we left the station when it stopped again."(Hardly 句首,倒装)
"One hour ___ and we had not gone far."("(时间)过去了"用动词哪个形式)
stage5.stem_cn: 一个小时过去了,我们没走多远。

stage5.stem: "The train rushed ___ the tiny station without stopping."("经过"用介词/副词哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 火车没停,从那小站呼啸而过。

stage5.stem: "We talked about times ___."("过去的(时光)"用哪个)
"The stationmaster ___ that the train existed."("否认(某事是真的)"用哪个)
"He ___ to help me with my complaint."("拒绝(做某事)"用 ___ to do)
"She ___ taking the money."("否认做过某事"用 ___ + 动名词)
"I ___ his copy of the schedule to check the time."("(从别人那)借入"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 我借来他那本时刻表查时间。

stage5.stem: "Could you ___ me your pen for a moment?"("把…借给别人"用哪个)
stage5.stem_cn: 你能把笔借给我用一下吗?

stage5.stem: "He ___ some money from a friend."("(向别人)借入"用哪个)

The stationmaster refused that the train existed.
